To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extinction time is approximately proportional to the product of population size, carrying capacity, and effective mutation load, and that the latter can be estimated from a single generation of data.

the expected extinction time of a population is approximately equal to the square of the effective mutation rate divided by the square of the selection coefficient, and that the coefficient of variation is typically less than 0·1.

the extinction time is approximately equal to 2.5 times the mean number of generations per deleterious mutation, and that the effective population size is approximately equal to the number of deleterious alleles that are segregating.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how selection and mutation interact to shape the genetic architecture of small populations.
the evolution of small populations and the extinction of clonal lineages.
a fundamental aspect of evolutionary theory: the joint action of mutation and selection in finite populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mutation load, in combination with the population size, determines the probability of extinction.
mutation load is not the only factor that limits the survival of small populations, but it is an important one, and its effects can be quite subtle.
the mutational meltdown is a real phenomenon, but it is not the most important factor determining extinction time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accumulation of mutations in finite populations is a much more complicated process than has generally been appreciated.
selection is more effective in reducing the mutational load when population size is small and the effects of mutations are large and highly variable.
mutation loads in finite populations are much smaller than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the survival of small populations is strongly influenced by the mutation load.
mutation load is a major determinant of population extinction.
the survival of small populations is strongly influenced by the joint action of mutation and selection, and that these processes are not independent.
